name: traversal-identity-create-address
description: The write-side half of the same rule: a change-set `create` whose element identity is a path traversal. A `create` is the one moment a client-supplied token contributes a path component, so this is the address at which admitting a traversal would actually write outside the layer directory — and it is refused by `$defs/identity` at the envelope, before any registry or authorization code runs.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model. The payload is an ordinary, schema-valid `implementation_types` value type and the approved scope covers the operation, so nothing but the identity is wrong: neither the payload check, nor the identity-conflict check, nor the authorization gate would have caught this one.

authorization.notes: A scope cannot express the traversal either — its `address.element` draws from the same `$defs/identity`, so there is no approval that could make this create legal.

expected.notes: The refusal is pass A, so the change set is never staged, never diffed and never authorized — and the real model is byte-identical for the ordinary reason that nothing before step 6 touches it. Note that the mismatch between the address identity and `value.name` is NOT what refuses this: that would be a semantic check the engine performs, and it must never be the only thing standing between a client and a write outside `model_root`.
